Weather is short-term; climate is the long-term average.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Climate is the long-term average of weather (usually 30+ years).

Climate change means these averages are shifting — temperatures, rainfall and seasons.

It is natural AND human-caused.

Solar energy enters the atmosphere and warms Earth's surface.

Some heat is re-radiated and trapped by greenhouse gases like CO₂, CH₄ and N₂O.

Without it Earth would be ~33°C colder!

Since 1850 global temperatures have risen by about 1.1°C.

The Paris Agreement (2015) aims to limit warming to 1.5°C above pre-industrial levels.

Beyond this, impacts become severe and irreversible.

mcqs.q: What is the enhanced greenhouse effect?
options: It is the hole in the ozone layer letting in more sun.
Climate change only happens in summer.
The strengthening of the natural greenhouse effect by human activities (mainly burning fossil fuels) which add CO2 and other gases to the atmosphere.
The greenhouse effect is entirely man-made and harmful.

mcqs.q: Why can a cold winter NOT disprove climate change?
options: Climate is the long-term statistical average; a single cold winter is a weather event. Climate change is the trend in averages and extremes over decades, not the absence of cold days.
Weather refers to rain and climate refers to temperature.
Climate change only happens in summer.
A really cold winter proves global warming is not happening.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between weather and climate?
options: Weather refers to rain and climate refers to temperature.
Weather happens outside and climate happens globally.
Climate change only happens in summer.
Weather is short-term atmospheric conditions at a specific time and place; climate is the long-term (typically 30-year) average of weather patterns in a region.
